subject: Re: Intro to economic buyer & procurement next steps - Solaris Innovations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lockhart <jamie.lockhart@solaris.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro & next steps after discovery call

Hi Jamie —

Thanks again for the chat earlier. Quick recap and a suggested next step so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from our call):
- Primary use case: inference at scale for customer-facing assistants (multi-tenant) with predictable latency and cost controls.
- Key constraints: on-prem procurement timeline, SOC2 evidence, and a likely requirement for an economic buyer sign-off from IT/Finance.
- Timeline: procurement kickoff target in ~6–8 weeks; pilot in Q3.

Can you introduce me to the economic buyer/budget owner who owns decisions for inference/infra spend? If procurement needs any initial security artifacts I can share our SOC2 summary and a draft master agreement.

Suggested next step: 30-min intro with the budget owner + procurement/legal to align on timeline and deliverables. We can include a short MLP (mutual action plan) and a pricing sketch.

If it's helpful, I can loop in our solutions lead (Alex Martinez) and our AE (Rishi Malhotra) to join the intro.

Thanks — appreciate the help here.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & next steps after discovery call

Hi Erin / Rebecca / Tim — nice to meet you over email and thanks Jamie for the intro.

Quick context: we help engineering teams run LLM inference with consistent latency and predictable unit economics across hosted/dedicated/private options. From our call with Jamie we think a 30-min alignment meeting will help confirm requirements for:

- Decision criteria (latency SLOs, data residency, PII/KMS needs)
- Procurement asks (SOC2 artifacts, draft contract terms, expected PO process)
- Budget/timing (who signs and expected procurement window)

Attached: SOC2-Summary.pdf (security snapshot) and a draft Redwood_MA-draft-v1.pdf for procurement to review.

Proposed slots (30 min):
- Tue Apr 6, 10:00–10:30 PT
- Tue Apr 6, 14:00–14:30 PT
- Wed Apr 7, 09:30–10:00 PT

Alex (solutions) and Rishi (AE) are on copy and can join the call. If you prefer, we can start synchronous or just share the short mutual action plan and timeline doc first.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm best slot for intro with Erin + procurement/legal.
2) Procurement to flag any must-have contract clauses or evidence you need before a commercial review.
3) If agreeable, we’ll share the MAP + a preliminary pricing sketch prior to the call.

Thanks — looking forward to coordinating.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: Solaris intro — prep checklist

Alex / Rishi — quick internal note after the intro thread with Solaris. Erin (budget owner) is on board to meet; procurement/legal are cc'd. Please see prep items below and let me know who can own which: 

Prep checklist:
- Alex: be ready to speak to deployment options (Dedicated vs Private), expected latency with multi-tenant configs, and a short demo of our ROI/cost controls.
- Rishi: bring a high-level pricing sketch and the pilot commercial structure we discussed (30–60 day pilot, skinnier commit).
- Marissa (me): draft mutual action plan and confirm meeting slots once Erin confirms availability.

Attachments to have ready: SOC2-Summary.pdf, Redwood_MA-draft-v1.pdf, one-pager pricing sketch.

I'll update the MAP doc in the shared link and send to the Solaris team before the call.

Thanks —
Marissa
